weeks.weekly_summary: Establish aerobic foundation with consistent easy runs and one tempo session. Focus on building running consistency after light recent volume.
weeks.coaching_notes: Recent Strava data shows only 8.4 km over 14 days — athlete is returning to training. Week 1 prioritizes consistency and aerobic base. days.notes: First hard session of block. Keep effort controlled; this sets the benchmark for future tempo work.

days.notes: First long run of block. Focus on time on feet and aerobic efficiency, not pace. Hydrate and fuel if running >90 min.

weeks.weekly_summary: Volume increases 8–10% to ~45.5 km. Introduce fartlek (unstructured speed play) as second quality session. Long run progresses to 14 km. Tempo drops to maintenance effort.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 2 increases volume within 10% rule (+3.5 km). Fartlek session on Tuesday (after easy Monday) adds variety and neuromotor stimulus without the rigidity of intervals. Tempo run shortened slightly to maintain aerobic focus. Long run +2 km follows sustainable progression. Monitor total weekly time budget (7 hrs) — should stay within range. HR patterns from Strava show good recovery capacity; maintain this momentum.
weeks.next_week_preview: Week 3 will push to ~48 km (peak volume before recovery week). Introduce short interval repeats and extend long run to 15–16 km. Maintain 2 quality sessions.

days.title: Tempo 7km (5:05/km)

days.notes: Slightly shorter than Week 1 tempo; focus on quality of effort at pace.

days.title: Long Run 14km (5:50/km)

days.notes: +2 km from Week 1. Fuel during run if taking >2 hours.

days.title: Easy 6km
days.description: Easy recovery run at 5:47–5:50/km. Day after long run.

days.title: Fartlek 8km (varied pace)
days.description: Warm-up 1 km easy (5:50/km). Then 6 km of unstructured fartlek: alternate 2–3 min at tempo effort (5:05/km, HR 160–165) with 90 sec recovery jog (5:50/km). Cool-down 1 km easy. Total: 5–6 surges.
days.key_focus: Aerobic power, lactate tolerance, pace awareness
days.notes: Second quality session of week. Less rigid than structured intervals; allows flexible intensity response.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Complete rest.

weeks.weekly_summary: Peak volume week (~48.5 km, +6.5% vs Week 2). Introduce short interval repeats (800m×6 @ 4:50/km) alongside tempo. Long run progresses to 15.5 km. This is the highest-volume week before recovery.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 3 is cumulative peak in this block. Two quality sessions with distinct stimulus: intervals (VO2 max) on Thursday, tempo focus on Tuesday. Long run +1.5 km builds endurance. Total volume +6.5% stays within 10% rule. Athlete should feel strong but not overly fatigued. If HR is elevated at rest (>55 bpm resting HR) or sleep is disrupted, reduce Wednesday run volume by 1–2 km. Monitor total fatigue score; if >75 by Friday, consider shortening Saturday easy run to facilitate recovery before Sunday long run.
weeks.next_week_preview: Week 4 is RECOVERY: volume drops 20–25% to ~36–37 km. Keep one quality session (maintenance tempo) but reduce long run by 20% (~12 km). This sets up for sustainable progression into the next training block.

days.title: Intervals 800m×6 (4:50/km)
days.description: Warm-up 1.5 km easy (5:50/km). Then 6 × 800m at 4:50/km (~3:52 per repeat) with 2 min recovery jog (5:50/km) between repeats. Cool-down 1 km easy. Target HR 170–178 bpm during repeats.
days.notes: First interval workout of block. Pace is ~12% faster than current easy pace; expect challenge. Shorter recovery between repeats builds capacity.

days.description: Easy recovery run at 5:47–5:50/km. Day after intervals.
days.notes: Keep effort light. HR should settle <150 bpm.

days.description: Sustained long run at 5:50/km. Strong aerobic effort, conversational pace throughout (HR 140–155 bpm). +1.5 km progression.
days.notes: Peak long run distance for this block. Fuel adequately; HR should be stable throughout.

days.title: Easy 6km
days.description: Easy recovery run at 5:47–5:50/km. Day after long run.

days.title: Tempo 6.5km (5:05/km)
days.description: Warm-up 1 km easy (5:50/km), then 4.5 km steady tempo at 5:05/km (lactate threshold), cool-down 1 km easy. Target HR 160–168 bpm.
days.key_focus: Lactate threshold maintenance, second quality session
days.notes: Shorter than Week 1–2 tempos but solid intensity. Maintains threshold fitness.

days.title: Easy 5.5km
days.description: Easy run at 5:47–5:50/km. Moderate distance to cap peak week without overload.
days.notes: Shorter than typical to prepare for recovery week and manage cumulative fatigue.

weeks.weekly_summary: RECOVERY WEEK: Volume drops 22% to ~37.8 km (down from 48.5 km Week 3). Maintain one quality session (moderate tempo) to preserve threshold fitness. Long run shortened by 20% to 12.5 km. Focus on consolidating gains and neural adaptation.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 4 is mandatory recovery to prevent overtraining and allow cumulative adaptation. Despite lower volume, maintain one quality session (Tuesday tempo) to preserve lactate threshold and prevent detraining. Long run shortened to 12.5 km (20% reduction). Easy runs are shorter across the week. HR should recover faster; resting HR may drop 2–3 bpm. This week sets the platform for the next 4-week training block, which will build intensity toward marathon-pace work. Athlete should feel fresher by Friday; use this as a signal that recovery is working.
weeks.next_week_preview: Next 4-week block (Weeks 5–8, Aerobic Development phase) will reintroduce longer tempos, marathon-pace segments in long runs, and progressive overload. Start that block with renewed freshness.

days.notes: Recovery week quality session. Shorter duration but solid intensity. Maintains threshold without overload.

coaching_overview: This 4-week Base Building block establishes aerobic foundation and introduces quality work. Athlete is returning from low recent volume (8.4 km / 14 days); Week 1 prioritizes consistency at easy pace (5:47–5:50/km) and one moderate tempo session. Volume progresses sustainably: Week 1 (42 km) → Week 2 (45.5 km, +8%) → Week 3 (48.5 km, +6.5%, peak) → Week 4 (37.8 km, −22%, recovery). Two quality sessions per week balance polarized training (80% easy / 20% hard). Long run grows from 12 km (Week 1) to 15.5 km (Week 3, peak), then recovers to 12.5 km (Week 4). All paces derived from Strava fitness: easy ~5:47/km, tempo ~5:05/km. Tempo and fartlek maintain lactate threshold; intervals (4:50/km repeats, Week 3) introduce VO2 max stimulus. Recovery week (Week 4) consolidates gains and resets fatigue. Athlete should complete this block with improved aerobic base, established tempo fitness, and readiness for Aerobic Development phase (Weeks 5–8), which will introduce marathon-pace segments and longer tempo efforts. Total plan distance: ~193 km over 4 weeks (average 48.25 km/week), fitting within 7-hour weekly time budget.
